reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: We pay for the streaming mix that gives our household the shows, movies, and sports we actually watch at a monthly price that feels worth it.

scenarios.label: Household core lineup
scenarios.description: A home decides which two or three services to keep year-round for everyday viewing.

scenarios.label: Family with kids
scenarios.description: Parents choose services anchored on children's programming, profiles, and controls that keep kids happy and safe.

scenarios.label: Carrier bundle activation
scenarios.description: A household activates a streaming service that comes included or discounted with a mobile/ISP plan and decides whether to keep it long term.

scenarios.label: Live sports season
scenarios.description: Fans subscribe for a league or event window and verify exact game rights, blackouts, and device support.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Household core lineup|generic] we keep flipping around at night and end up renting random movies or rewatching the same shows. want one dependable place the whole house uses, not five bills and three remotes. what should i be doing differently?

[problem_recognition|Family with kids|generic] my 7 and 10 year old keep clicking into stuff i don't want them seeing. i need a safe corner with age limits and lots of kid shows, but also something decent for parents after bedtime. how do people set this up?

[problem_recognition|Carrier bundle activation|generic] my phone plan says it includes some video perk i never turned on. is it even worth it, and how do i activate it without getting surprise charges?

[problem_recognition|Live sports season|generic] season starts soon and i'm going to miss games if i don't sort this. need near-live feeds (minimal delay), 4k when available, and a way to watch on the living room tv and my phone. what do fans use for this?
[discovery|Household core lineup|generic] what's the best streaming option for a household core lineup - weeknight series plus weekend movies, easy on a living room tv, not a mess of add-ons?
[discovery|Family with kids|generic] best family-friendly streaming for kids under 10 with strong parental controls, downloads for trips, and enough grownup shows for us too?
[discovery|Carrier bundle activation|generic] best streaming choices that often come bundled with phone plans, and how to get the most value from a free or discounted perk?
[discovery|Live sports season|generic] best streaming setup for live sports season with low latency, 4k when offered, solid dvr, and reliable apps on a smart tv and phone. what should i look at?
[shortlist|Household core lineup|generic] can you give me 3 or 4 top options to anchor our household lineup for series and movies, with quick pros and cons?
[shortlist|Family with kids|generic] shortlist 3 kid-friendly options with strong parental controls and lots of animated shows, but still enough adult series for parents.

[shortlist|Carrier bundle activation|generic] i have a carrier perk to activate. give me a short list of a few common bundled subscriptions worth using for series and movies, plus what to check in the fine print when i turn it on.

[shortlist|Live sports season|generic] for this season, can you list 3 or 4 ways to watch most games without cable, prioritized for low delay, 4k availability, and device support for a living room tv and a phone?

[criteria|Household core lineup|generic] trying to pick a couple streamers for our home base. what should I actually weigh besides price? stuff like catalog depth, profiles, 4K, downloads, simultaneous streams, app reliability?

[criteria|Family with kids|generic] Kids are 4 and 8. What matters most for a family streaming service so I am not constantly policing it? solid parental controls, real kids profiles by age, disable autoplay, easy downloads for trips?

[criteria|Carrier bundle activation|generic] My phone plan includes a streaming perk. Before I activate it, what should I look for? is it tied to my number, can I link an existing account, which tier it unlocks, any traps with billing if I change carriers later?

[criteria|Live sports season|generic] Setting up for the season. What should I prioritize in a sports streamer? blackout rules and local access, 4K at 60fps, low latency, DVR depth, multiview, and honestly the feel of the broadcasts and pregame shows matter too.

[feature_screening|Live sports season|generic] Which streaming options actually support multiview (3-4 live games at once) and true 4K 60fps, plus a cloud DVR that lets me start from the beginning and fast forward through commercials on TV apps?

[use_case|Household core lineup|generic] Cutting cable. I want a simple setup: one main service for new series and movies, maybe one add-on for occasional sports, must work on two TVs and a couple iPads, easy for parents to use, and keep it under about 30 a month. How would you build that?

[use_case|Family with kids|generic] Road trips and after school screen time. Need a service where I can lock kids profiles to a 5-8 age range, turn off autoplay, download a bunch of episodes to tablets, and keep mature stuff off the home screen. What settings or picks make this painless?

[use_case|Carrier bundle activation|generic] I already pay for a streaming account, and my wireless plan now offers the same service free. How do I activate through the carrier without losing my watchlist or getting double billed, and can I switch it back if I change carriers?

[use_case|Live sports season|generic] Hosting watch nights this season. Two TVs inside plus a projector outside. I want low delay streams, multiview for early games, and a DVR that records every game for my team and lets me skip ads. Needs to work on a set-top box and a streaming stick. Walk me through the setup and settings to make that smooth.
[social_validation|-|generic] What do people actually rave about in their go-to streaming service right now? not specs on paper, the stuff that makes them feel good keeping it month after month.

[comparison|Household core lineup|Disney+] netflix or disney+ for our main household lineup? adults + occasional family night. where do they really differ, especially on originals and day-to-day stuff?

[comparison|Family with kids|Amazon Prime Video] For kids 6 and 9 plus parents, how does Netflix stack up against Amazon Prime Video? I care about kids profiles, parental controls, offline downloads for tablets, dubs/subs on cartoons, and how deep the kids library actually is.

[comparison|Carrier bundle activation|Hulu] My phone plan includes Hulu. If I activate it, do I still need Netflix or would Hulu cover most of our watching? What would I actually miss from Netflix that might make paying for both worth it?

[comparison|Live sports season|Max] Locking in my setup for the season. Between Netflix and Max, which fits better for sports nights and sports-adjacent stuff? Thinking live games vs shoulder programming, 4K availability, stream limits, latency feel on a big screen, and overall vibe for watch parties.

[objections|Household core lineup|generic] Netflix keeps creeping up in price and it's our most expensive app now. For a core household lineup, is it really earning its keep or should we rotate it off for a while?

[objections|Family with kids|generic] We mostly use Netflix for a couple kids shows and a weekend movie. Price is getting high for that. Is keeping Netflix for the kids a bad spend if we barely touch the rest?

[objections|Carrier bundle activation|generic] I just got a carrier bundle discounting our streaming. Keeping Netflix on top of that feels like I'm double paying. Is there a solid reason not to drop Netflix right now?

[objections|Live sports season|generic] I'm budgeting for the season and prices are up everywhere. If my priority is games and pregame shows, is Netflix worth keeping during the sports months or is that money better pushed to more sports-heavy options?

[pricing|Household core lineup|generic] What's a sensible monthly budget for a core streaming mix without overpaying, and do ad tiers usually come out cheaper than ad-free for a couple that watches about 10 hours a week?

[pricing|Family with kids|generic] For a family of 4 with two kid profiles, what's the cheapest Netflix plan that still allows two streams at once, 4K if possible, and downloads for a road trip? Do kids profiles show ads on the ad plan?

[pricing|Carrier bundle activation|generic] My wireless plan already covers one streaming service. If I add Netflix, is it cheaper to bill through the carrier or direct, and are there gotchas with promos or losing discounts later?

[pricing|Live sports season|generic] I only want subscriptions during the season. How low can I keep costs if I rotate month to month, and where does Netflix land on monthly price, 4K add-ons, and pausing or canceling without extra fees?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] I've had Netflix forever, but lately we finish one show then it just sits. Should I pause or cancel Netflix for a bit, or is there a smarter way to keep it without paying for weeks we don't use it?
[alternatives|-|defensive] thinking about canceling Netflix this month. if I bail, what services should I try instead so I'm not missing too much?
[alternatives|-|Disney+] If I drop Disney+, what should I get instead for family movies and some sci-fi and animated series?
[alternatives|-|Amazon Prime Video] I barely use Amazon Prime Video anymore. If I cancel it, what's a better service for movies and a few big original shows?
[alternatives|-|Hulu] My Hulu promo's ending and the price jumps. What should I switch to that covers current TV and lots of comedies?
[alternatives|-|Max] I'm pausing Max now that I finished the big HBO shows. What other service would scratch that prestige drama plus blockbuster movie vibe?
[renewal|-|generic] My Netflix renews next week. Is it still worth keeping at this price, or should I drop to the ad plan or swap to something cheaper for a bit?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] Netflix keeps throwing a "too many people are watching" error even when it's just me at home after that household change. How do I fix this so it works on my TV and my phone?
[expansion|-|generic] I'm happy with Netflix and thinking about upgrading to 4K and adding an extra member for my sister. Any gotchas, or a smarter way to set this up across two homes?

[ecosystem|-|generic] What apps or gadgets pair well with Netflix to make finding stuff easier and do watch parties? I've got a Roku in the living room, an older Samsung TV in the bedroom, and a laptop.
[advocacy|-|generic] My friend keeps saying Netflix isn't worth it anymore. How do I make a solid case for keeping it without sounding salesy? What points actually land?
